Subject: Plan selection: untangling upgrade paths from Compact to High-Throughput

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency improvements look promising. We reviewed our Q3 usage and think we'll need to move off the Compact plan sooner than expected because a new imaging pipeline will increase token volume and concurrency.

A few concrete questions from engineering and procurement:
- Do you offer a staged upgrade (Compact -> Mid -> High-Throughput) with proration for mid-quarter moves?
- Can we bundle the Optimize add-on (automatic batching suggestions + quantization recommendations) and get a single blended price?
- Are there discounts for a 12-month commit vs month-to-month for dedicated capacity?

I've attached our usage CSV (ava_usage_report_q3.csv) — summary: ~1.8B tokens/month with peak concurrency ~150 requests/min, p95 generation length ~420 tokens. Our procurement lead (cc'd on later threads) will want to understand billing cadence and how feature entitlements transfer if we switch plans mid-contract.

Can you outline options and a rough cost delta for moving to High-Throughput vs keeping Compact with burst capacity? Happy to set a quick call.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhou
Head of ML Engineering, AvaMed Diagnostics
emily@avamed.com

Subject: Re: Plan selection: untangling upgrade paths from Compact to High-Throughput

Hi Emily — thanks for the usage file, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front, then a suggested path: 

Short answer: yes to staged upgrades and blended bundles, with pricing tradeoffs depending on committed capacity and features.

Options we typically recommend for customers in your usage band:
1) Step upgrade (Compact -> Mid -> High)
   - Fastest from a rollout perspective, preserves existing entitlements, billing is prorated at the month level.
   - If you need immediate throughput, we can add a short-term burst pool for the month of transition.
2) Parallel pilot + cutover
   - Spin up a High-Throughput pool in parallel for a pilot workload (recommended if you want zero-risk validation). Billing is separate until you cut over.
3) Compact + Elastic Burst + Optimize add-on
   - If you prefer to defer a full upgrade, the Elastic Burst add-on buys headroom for peaks and comes with the Optimize bundle (auto-batching suggestions). Cheaper but may not hit p99 targets at highest concurrency.

Pricing & discounts: for a 12-month committed reserved capacity we typically provide a tiered discount; for a commitment level that covers ~70% of your projected tokens we can offer a 15–22% list discount depending on GPU profile and quantization choices. I've attached a proposed tier worksheet (proposed_tier_pricing_worksheet.xlsx) with example numbers — this is intentionally high-level so we can tune it on a call.

Operational notes:
- Feature bundling: Optimize and SLA 99.9 are add-ons that can be bundled into a single PO; entitlements move with the customer as long as the SOW calls them out.
- Proration: we prorate at the day-level for Dedicated capacity moves; licenses are creditable if you sign a backstop commitment.

Can you confirm: target p99 latency, acceptable cost uplift (percent), and whether procurement requires a capped monthly spend vs. usage-based? Then I can send a concrete 2-option quote (pilot route vs direct upgrade) and propose next steps (call + SOW).

Thanks — looping Karthik (pricing) and Laura (customer success) to help scope the SOW and run the pricing worksheet with you.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Thanks — that framing helps. A few clarifications from our side:
- p99 latency target: <= 150ms for the majority of inference (we can accept occasional spikes during heavy imaging batch runs).
- Cost sensitivity: procurement prefers a capped monthly spend or a hard cap on burst charges; month-to-month variability is a blocker for them.
- Timeline: want pilot within 6 weeks, production cutover within 12 weeks if pilot is successful.

Procurement has asked specifically about proration on mid-quarter upgrades and whether credits apply if we downgrade after a pilot. They also asked for typical SLA escalations and a sample SOW.

Samir (cc) is our procurement consultant and will coordinate contract language. Samir — we discussed a couple of vendor options and Redwood is preferred for serving latency. Could you share the standard procurement questions you need answered?

Appreciate the proposed worksheet — we can walk through numbers on a call.

Best,
Emily

Hi Emily, Samir — looping in final recommendations and a proposed next step list after syncing with pricing and CS.

Recommendation (short): run a 4-week pilot on a High-Throughput pool for a representative imaging workload, with Compact retained for lower-priority pipelines during the pilot. If pilot meets p99 <=150ms, sign a 12-month reserved capacity SOW covering ~70% of forecast tokens.

Why this path:
- Pilot validates latency and KV-cache behavior with minimal risk.
- Parallel pilot simplifies rollback (no in-place migration risk).
- A 12-month commit lets us offer an introductory uplift discount — for your commitment level and GPU choice we can provide a 20% list discount and waive first-month burst charges for the pilot.

Pricing examples (illustrative, final numbers in SOW):
- Pilot (4 weeks): Dedicated High-Throughput pool (pilot size 1x c48 equivalent) — estimated incremental cost: $18k for pilot month (waived with commitment).
- Production reserved (12-month commit at 70% forecast): Monthly effective cost ≈ $42k after 20% discount (includes Optimize add-on and 99.9 SLA).
- Compact + Elastic Burst alternative: Monthly cost ≈ $28k + capped burst credit (if you prefer a capped spend we can set an alert threshold and hard cap mechanism).

Contract & operational notes:
- Proration: Day-level proration on Dedicated capacity; credits apply for downgrades if you exit within 30 days of upgrade (standard credit schedule in SOW).
- Bundled entitlements (Optimize + SLA) will be listed as line items on the SOW and carry over with the reserved capacity; if you downgrade within the committed term, entitlements are reduced per the SOW.
- Procurement requests: we'll provide a sample SOW, SOC2 evidence, and escalation matrix. Attached is a high-level SLA summary (redwood_sla_summary.pdf).

Next steps:
1) Quick alignment call (30m) this week to confirm targets and finalize pilot size — propose Fri 4:00 PM PT.
2) I’ll produce two SOW drafts: (A) Pilot + 12-month reserved path, (B) Compact + Elastic Burst + Optimize.
3) If pilot is green, sign SOW via DocuSign (link below) and schedule provisioning.

DocuSign (draft SOW): https://docusign.com/sow/AVAMED-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/AVAMED-2027-Q4

If monthly capped spend is a hard requirement, we can structure the reserved capacity with an Overhead Buffer and a monthly cap — will confirm with legal on exact language.

Would you and Samir be available at Fri 4:00 PM PT? If not, suggest two windows and we’ll accommodate.

All best,
